item.title: Teen cannabis use linked to flattened cognitive development in large U.S. study
item.dc:creator: Eric W. Dolan
item.description:
Adolescents who started using cannabis early showed slower gains on memory and attention tests over four years.

The post Teen cannabis use linked to flattened cognitive development in large U.S. study appeared first on PsyPost - Psychology News.
item.content:encoded:
Adolescents who started using cannabis early showed slower gains on memory and attention tests over four years, according to new research published in JAMA Psychiatry. The findings come from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, which follows thousands of children across 21 sites in the United States.

“We wanted to know whether the differences seen in earlier, smaller studies held up when you follow the same young people over time,” said study author Jane Roe of the University of Minnesota.

The researchers compared 412 teens who reported using cannabis before age 15 with matched peers who did not. Earlier work had linked heavy use to lower scores (see a 2026 review), but causality remains debated.

The study, “Cannabis Initiation and Cognitive Trajectories in Adolescence,” was authored by Jane Roe, Ahmed Khan, and Lisa Park.

item.title: Psilocybin shows early promise for lingering Lyme disease symptoms
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Hedrih
item.description: A small open-label trial found that two psilocybin sessions with psychological support were followed by less fatigue and pain in people with post-treatment Lyme disease.
item.content:encoded:
A small open-label trial found that two psilocybin sessions with psychological support were followed by less fatigue and pain in people with post-treatment Lyme disease. The study was published in Journal of Psychopharmacology.

Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome affects a minority of patients after antibiotic therapy, and few treatments exist. Twenty participants completed the protocol; symptom scores fell by about a third at the eight-week follow-up.

The study, “Psilocybin-assisted therapy for post-treatment Lyme disease: an open-label pilot,” was authored by Albert Garcia-Romeu and colleagues.

item.title: Semaglutide users report fewer alcohol cravings, survey finds
item.dc:creator: Eric W. Dolan
item.description: People taking GLP-1 drugs described a drop in the urge to drink.
item.content:encoded:
People taking GLP-1 drugs described a drop in the urge to drink in an online survey of 1,100 adults.

The paper is available online (doi: 10.1038/s41380-026-03312-7).
